newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Analysts comments on Dutch PTT results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts comments on Dutch PTT results.

text.p: Dutch post and telecoms group PTT Nederland NV posted 1996 net profit of 2.46 billion guilders versus a previous 2.26 billion. The profit was in line with analysts expectations.
The dividend was set at 2.85 guilders/share. PTT also said it expected further growth in net income in 1997.
Below are some analysts' comments on the results:
RENE VERHOEF OF NIBSTRATING SECURITIES
"The figures and forecast are in line with expectations and the dividend of 2.85 guilders per share was just below our estimate.
"The dip in the share price after the figures is overdone, since the stock was up before (the announcement) and the profits and outlook did not disappoint."
PATRICK WOLLENBERG AT IRIS:
"The figures -- turnover, net profit, dividend, operational profit -- are very much in line with expectations. They're just fine.
"The prospects are OK as well. There's no reason to adjust my "Buy" recomendation, although I might do some fine-tuning after the analyst meeting tomorrow."
STEVEN VROLIJK OF ING BARINGS:

"KPN forecasts more growth for 1997 which is good, but it would be interesting to hear how they intend to boost sales in the telecoms sector as competition will become harder as new competitors enter the (Dutch) market with continuing deregulation.

"The (profit) contribution of TNT is likely to be small in 1997. But, post -- a sector which accounts for about 50 percent of total turnover since the acquisition of TNT -- should show a stable increase in profits. We'll stick to our "Buy" recommendation."
ARJEN DIBBETS at MEES PIERSON:

"They delivered as they said they would. Operating income was exactly according to expectations, but, on the financial side, the tax bill was 50 million (guilders) better, while interest charges were 30 million worse (than expected)...

"For the future, it's not really exciting. We don't expect EPS growth to accelerate in the next two years. We don't see a short-term drama from competition, but we also think there are no more significant gains from restructuring...
"KPN (stock) has underperformed. We had it as a "Hold" and I can't see that changing."
JOOST VAN BEEK AT VAN MEER JAMES CAPEL:
"The figures are in line with our expectations, more important is their quality and composition.

"Postal activities seem to have done very well. Efficiency has increased, the hike in mail tariffs may have helped to lift income...Overall a nice increase in gross margin to some 14 percent at postal activities.

"I am positively surprised they give a clear forecast on earnings for this year. As full competition in fixed-line telephony starts this year, I did not expect them to say much on 1997 developments before the release of the half year results."
